page: Microsoft Azure E2s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Esv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8573C processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The configuration includes 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. No local storage is bundled, though the instance is Premium Storage capable, and it does not include any GPUs.

Performance benchmarks reveal a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core performance is notable, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2149.0, categorized as strong, and an average stress-ng single-core CPU performance of 1942.19. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are more constrained. The stress-ng multi-core performance is poor at 1991.97, and the Geekbench multi-core score is weak at 2641.0. Memory bandwidth for large blocks is poor, registering at 21.51 GB/sec for read operations and 14.04 GB/sec for write operations.

From a workload perspective, the E2s_v6 is suited for memory-intensive tasks that do not require heavy parallelization or high multi-core throughput. It achieves average performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 31.03 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression at 13.13 GB/sec. It is also capable of handling light database operations and text processing, though its Redis SET performance is poor at 2.56 million operations per second. This instance represents a cost-efficient entry point for memory-optimized workloads requiring moderate compute power but a larger memory footprint per core.

Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this x86_64 instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs from a single physical core and 16.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per core memory density. It features no local storage but is Premium Storage capable, and lacks GPU resources. Benchmarks indicate strong single-core performance, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2149.0, though multi-core and memory bandwidth results are generally weak to poor. The instance is best suited for memory-intensive, low-concurrency workloads such as light database operations, single-threaded file compression, and basic text processing where a high memory-to-vCPU ratio is required without the need for extensive multi-threaded compute power.
